messages:
Mina: Ran a quick nsys profile on the serving runtime this morning. seeing repeated spikes where queue_time >> compute_time for medium batches (batch_size 8, seq 2048). trace attached but TL;DR looks like ordering + KV cache misses interacting with batching window.

Raj: can you paste the nsys command you used?

Mina: sure —
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas,osrt --sample=none -o run_kvcache_batch --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-include=1 ./server --config prod_batch.json
```

Mina: exported the .qdrep -> perfetto and inspected kernel timeline. top timeline oddities: repeated small memcpy H2D and device kernel launches between attention matmuls when KV cache miss rate > 30%.

perf-bot: nsys summary: total GPU time 48s, memcpy H2D 6.5s (13.5%), cudaLaunch overhead 2.1s, small kernels (<1ms) account for 22% of GPU time.

Eve: interesting. did you correlate with queueing windows? continuous batching disabled?

Mina: continuous batching was enabled with window_ms=12. but the sampling of incoming request sizes created frequent micro-batches: 3–4 requests in quick succession then idle. when a new request misses KV cache we do a copy of the whole cached KV slab -> triggers memcpy and kernel syncs.

Cameron: that matches the pattern I saw in perfetto: matmul blocks separated by 2-3 memcpy events and small kernels. looks like our kernel selection path chooses the same kernel variant for cached vs uncached path but we pay extra overhead on miss path.

Raj: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? even approximate names helps.

Mina: timeline snippet (abbreviated):
```
[0ms] matmul_attn_fwd_k    2.3ms
[2.3ms] memcpy_h2d         0.7ms
[3.0ms] kv_apply_kernel    0.9ms
[3.9ms] matmul_attn_fwd_k  2.1ms
[6.0ms] cudaLaunch         0.1ms
[6.1ms] small_reduce_k     0.4ms
[6.5ms] memcpy_h2d         0.6ms
[7.1ms] matmul_attn_fwd_k  2.4ms
```

Eve: notice the memcpy_h2d between matmuls — that suggests we can't reuse device KV memory across the micro-batch boundary. is our KV layout pinned GPU memory or staged from host?

Mina: pinned GPU for cached, but on miss we reconstruct slab on host then memcpy into device. we do this under the request lock so it serializes with the batch processing thread.

Cameron: two knobs to try: 1) prefetch new KV entries asynchronously into device memory outside the critical path, 2) bump continuous batching window to 20ms to amortize memcpy across more requests.

Raj: also consider switching kernel selection heuristics: pick kernel variants that are more tolerant to cache misses (fewer small kernels) even if single-kernel compute a bit slower — reduces kernel launch overhead.

Mina: agree. ran a quick A/B locally: window_ms=12 vs 24 on synthetic trace with 35% KV miss rate -> p50 similar, p95 improved by ~18% with 24ms, but p99 slightly worse for cold-start single-request latency.

perf-bot: regression check: turning on async prefetch + window_ms=24 reduced memcpy H2D time from 13% -> 5% and reduced small-kernel fraction from 22% -> 9% in a 1min run.

Eve: tradeoff noted: higher window increases tail for single cold requests. For PLG customers we care about tail. maybe we need adaptive windowing: small window when requests sparse, expand when throughput picks up.

Mina: prototype idea: maintain EWMA of inter-arrival time per-route. if ia_ewma < threshold -> expand window to W_high, else shrink to W_low. also asynchronously prefetch predicted KV ids using LRU+lookahead.

Cameron: sounds good. can you open a GH issue with the nsys traces and the perfetto link + exact config? I can try the async prefetch patch.

Mina: opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4621 — includes qdrep + perfetto link + short reproducible driver. tagging @Cameron @Eve.

Raj: next steps: Cameron to prototype async prefetch, Mina to implement adaptive window EWMA, Eve to run long-run nsys on canary with mixed traffic. sync early next week?

Cameron: on it. will post a short microbenchmark and kernel-filtered nsys output here. :thumbsup:

Eve: I'll schedule a 30m perf session Mon 10am to run 30m traces and collect p50/95/99 and kernel breakdowns.

Mina: thanks team. main takeaway: KV cache misses are amplifying kernel-launch/memcpy overhead under our current batching heuristics. mitigations: async prefetch, adaptive batching windows, and possibly choosing kernel variants with fewer small kernels to reduce launch overhead.

Raj: nice work — feels like a clear ownerable path. adding to eng-runtime sprint backlog. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
